Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 25-Nov-2025 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  THIRD SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  SUBJECT: CSS 2103/CSS_2103 DATA ANALYTICS  
 (SPL: COMPUTER SCIENCE AND ENGINEERING / ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE / CYBER SECURITY / DATA SCIENCE /  
  INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY)  
  DATA ANALYTICS [CSS 2103]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                      Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)               The Glossary manager wants to boost the basket value and reduce missed cross-sell opportunities. (5)  
  The manager believes that certain items, such as milk, bread, cheese, butter, eggs, bananas, and  
  coffee, are frequently bought together; these items should be co-located on the shelves. For this  
  scenario, apply the Apriori algorithm to verify that buying patterns are interesting to the users.  
  Consider the following transaction logs shown in Table Q.1A  
  Answer the followings(candidate set represented as C, Frequent itemset represented as L):  
  
  
  i. Build C₁ → L₁, C₂ → L₂, C₃ → L₃ with min support count = 4; list pruned candidates at each stage.  
  ii. Generate rules from the largest Lk with min_conf = 70%;  
  Compute support, confidence. If min_sup changes to 5, which itemsets drop? Briefly explain via the  
  Apriori property.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
1B)               A medical equipment company claims that its new blood test kit has an average accuracy rate of          (3)  
  95%. A quality inspector believes the true accuracy may be different from the claimed value (it  
  could be higher or lower). To verify the claim, a random sample of 36 test kits is taken, and the  
  sample shows an average accuracy of 94.7% with a known population standard deviation of  
  0.02. At the 5% significance level, test whether the company's claim is justified. (critical z-values  
  are ±1.96)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  Page #1

1C)   An ice cream manufacturer noticed that sales of ice cream increase every summer and drop in         (2)  
  winter. The sales pattern repeats each year with increasing average sales overtime due to  
  marketing efforts. Which components are present in this time series? Identify the time series model  
  that would best represent this pattern and why?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2A)   Table Q. 2A shown below has the data collected during the outbreak of smallpox.                      (5)  
  
  
  Test the effectiveness of vaccination in preventing smallpox at 5% significance level.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2B)   Consider frequent 1-itemsets:                                                                        (3)  
  $$L_{1} = {A, B, C, D, E, F}.$$  
  Use the hash function  
  
  
  and the following transactions:  
  T₁: {A, B, C}  
  T₂: {A, D, E}  
  T₃: {B, C, E, F}  
  T₄: {A, B, E, F}.  
  i. Construct the hash table H₂ showing bucket addresses, counts, and contents.  
  ii. If the minimum support is 4, which buckets can be pruned?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2C)   Two forecasting models for production planning are evaluated as follows:                             (2)  
  
  
  Justify and explain which model gives better overall forecasting performance? Explain, considering  
  all measures  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3A)   i.Find the standard deviation and skewness for the following data:                                   (5)  
  78, 91, 68, 54, 82, 47, 60, 78, 97, 58, 62, 50, 50, 63, 92, 75 79, 63, 42, 61  
  ii. Give example for "Combining variables" concept in dataset preparation.  
  iii. A CMO of a company marketing carbonated soft drinks has developed three new flavors of cola  
  and decided to measure the customers' preference for these three flavors from 12 customers by  
  using scale of 1 to 9. The table of data is shown below. Conduct the appropriate analysis here.  
  
  
  Page #2

Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3B)   A dataset contains 100 transactions.                                                                 (3)  
  • 20 transactions include both {Pen, Notebook}.  
  • 25 transactions include {Pen}.  
  • 40 transactions include {Notebook}.  
  i. Calculate Support and Confidence for the rule {Pen} → {Notebook}.  
  ii. If the minimum support is 10% and minimum confidence is 60%, check whether the rule is  
  strong.  
  iii. Interpret the result.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3C)   Consider the sales for the past 5 weeks: 120, 130, 125, 140, 150.                                    (2)  
  i. Compute the 3-week Simple Moving Average (SMA) forecast for week 6.  
  ii. Comment briefly on the difference between the SMA and WMA forecasts.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4A)   Given the following transaction database:                                                            (5)  
  
  
  a) Convert the above database into vertical data format and find all frequent itemsets with a  
  minimum support of 2.  
  b) List the advantages of using vertical data format over horizontal format in frequent itemset  
  mining?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4B)   A company tracks monthly sales (in units) for a product:                                             (3)  
  
  
  Page #3

Using Single Exponential Smoothing (SES) with a smoothing constant α = 0.3, and assuming the  
  forecast for Month 1 is 120 units,  
  (a) Calculate the forecast for Months 2 to 6.  
  (b) Compute the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) for the forecasts from Months 2 to 5.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4C)   A supermarket's market-basket analysis generates several association rules, such as:                     (2)  
  $$• Rule 1: Diapers → Beer (support = 5\%, confidence = 80\%)$$  
  $$• Rule 2: Milk → Bread (support = 20\%, confidence = 60\%)$$  
  Some rules may appear strong based on support and confidence but can be misleading.  
  a. Explain why some association rules can be misleading even if they have high support and  
  confidence.  
  b. Identify at least two additional measures that can be used to evaluate the true strength of a rule.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
5A)   A transportation company tracks its monthly passenger counts (Yt). The data for the first five           (5)  
  months are given. Applying Holt's Method  
  
  
  Parameters: Use smoothing constants  
  a. Calculate the initial Level (L1 ) and Trend (T2 ).  
  b. Calculate the final Level (L5 ) and Trend (T5 ) based on all five data points.  
  c. Use L5 and T5 to provide the forecast for Month 7 (F7 ).  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5B)   An online electronics store analysed 1,000 customer purchase transactions. The following data            (3)  
  were obtained:  
  
  
  Page #4

(a) Calculate the pattern evaluation measures such as Lift, Kulc and cosine for the following  
  association rule:  
  Smartphone→WirelessEarbuds  
  (b) Justify the relationship between Smartphone and Earbud purchases based on the obtained Lift  
  and Kulc values.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5C)                   A data analyst is studying the annual income levels (in ₹000s) of 12 employees in a company:        (2)  
  [180, 200, 210, 215, 220, 230, 250, 270, 300, 320, 400, 480]  
  Apply both equal-width and equal-frequency binning with 3 bins.  
  Using histogram analysis, discuss which binning approach (equal-width or equal-frequency)  
  provides a better representation of the income distribution and justify your reasoning.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"
